purpose: Six Founder decisions required before any destructive MAINT-01 cleanup proceeds
source: maint01_founder_decision_register_v2.json — extracted and enriched for Founder review
note: These six decisions are grouped to minimize decision burden. No action from Jackie is required beyond answering these six items.

decisions.title: Foundation Communication Site — retain or consolidate
decisions.plain_english_question: Should the standalone Foundation communication site (foundation_comm) be kept as a separate public-facing site, or merged into the main Foundation team site (foundation_div) and retired?

current_state.type: Standalone SharePoint communication site (no Team, no M365 Group)

decisions.why_this_exists: Communication sites in SharePoint are typically used for intranet landing pages, public informational portals, or division home pages. This site likely predates the Foundation Team site (foundation_div) or was created for a specific public-facing purpose. With no Team or Group backing, it exists outside the standard collaboration structure.
decisions.recommendation: CONSOLIDATE — migrate Programs & Events content to sites/foundation_div and retire the standalone site. Two Foundation sites with overlapping content and unclear authority creates confusion. foundation_div is the Team-connected, governed operational site.

alternatives.RETAIN: If foundation_comm serves as the public-facing/external-audience Foundation portal (e.g., grant applicants or donors land here), it should be retained. Jackie must document its distinct public purpose and distinguish it from foundation_div.
alternatives.CONSOLIDATE: If foundation_comm is an orphaned legacy site duplicating what foundation_div already does, migrate Programs & Events content to foundation_div and retire the standalone site.

decisions.if_approved: Authorizes Wave 6 Step 1: content migration from foundation_comm to foundation_div, read-only hold for 30 days, then site retirement.
decisions.if_deferred: Both Foundation sites remain active with no documented purpose distinction. Canon confusion continues.
decisions.cost_impact: Low — standalone SharePoint sites carry minimal incremental cost
decisions.operational_impact: Low — Programs & Events content migrated to foundation_div is accessible in the same tenant
decisions.consequence_of_deferral: Duplicate Foundation sites with unclear authority remain indefinitely
decisions.approval_phrase: APPROVE FD-001 — CONSOLIDATE foundation_comm into foundation_div and retire

decisions.title: Enterprise canon location — single authoritative store
decisions.plain_english_question: Which SharePoint location is the single authoritative home for enterprise governance documents: ImplementationHQ/Architecture/00_CANON, or both ImplementationHQ and the publishing site's Enterprise Governance folder equally?

current_state.location_a: sites/ImplementationHQ — Shared Documents/Architecture/00_CANON (active, last modified Jul 2026)
current_state.location_b: sites/publishing — Shared Documents/JM1 Shared Services/Enterprise Governance (active, last modified Jul 2026)
current_state.overlap: PROGRAM-004 entity evidence and enterprise governance documents exist in both locations

decisions.why_this_exists: Both ImplementationHQ (architecture/governance hub) and the publishing site (operational document store) have evolved to store enterprise-scope governance materials. This creates two competing locations for the same authoritative documents.
decisions.recommendation: OPTION A — ImplementationHQ/Architecture/00_CANON is the single authoritative enterprise canon. The publishing site's Enterprise Governance folder becomes a clearly labeled reference copy with a pointer note. No files need to be deleted — only a governance label added.

alternatives.OPTION_A: ImplementationHQ/00_CANON is the single source. Publishing copy becomes a reference with a header note pointing to ImplementationHQ.
alternatives.OPTION_B: Both are co-equal for their respective scopes (architecture vs. publishing-specific evidence). Requires explicit documented split-scope rule to prevent drift.

decisions.if_approved: Adds a reference header to publishing/Enterprise Governance folder. No files deleted or moved. Prevents future version drift.
decisions.if_deferred: Editors and automation may continue writing to the wrong location, creating document version drift between sites.
decisions.operational_impact: Low — governance/labeling decision only. No file moves required.
decisions.consequence_of_deferral: Canon duplication continues; document authority is ambiguous
decisions.approval_phrase: APPROVE FD-002 — ImplementationHQ/Architecture/00_CANON is the authoritative enterprise canon; publishing copy becomes reference

decisions.title: sites/projects — remove legacy dev artifact content
decisions.plain_english_question: Should the stale developer build artifacts (JavaScript bundles, repository mirrors, build outputs) stored in SharePoint's Projects site be archived or removed, now that GitHub and the App Service estate are the authoritative code stores?

current_state.content: JS bundles, Next.js build outputs, branch checkouts (jm1-agape, jmerrill-pub), SECURITY.md mirrors
current_state.size: Large drive — exact size not measured but multiple repo mirrors

decisions.why_this_exists: During early development, dev artifacts were stored in SharePoint as a staging area or secondary copy. Since HOST-02 is complete and GitHub is the canonical code store, these SharePoint copies are stale and no longer needed in production.
decisions.recommendation: OPTION A — archive or remove build artifacts from SharePoint. Keep the Projects Team shell if any actual planning/coordination happens there (addressed in FD-006). Verify no CI/CD pipeline references sites/projects before removing anything.

alternatives.OPTION_A: ARCHIVE/CLEAN — remove or archive dev build artifacts. Retain Team shell pending FD-006.
alternatives.OPTION_B: RETAIN AS-IS — leave SharePoint dev store as historical snapshot. No immediate cleanup.
alternatives.OPTION_C: RETIRE FULLY — retire both content and Projects Team/site if Projects collaboration has fully ended.

decisions.if_approved: Authorizes Wave 6 Step 2: verify no CI/CD references, create archive ZIP of unique non-GitHub content, remove stale artifacts from SharePoint.
decisions.if_deferred: Stale dev artifacts remain in SharePoint, creating potential confusion about canonical code locations. Storage cost continues.
decisions.security_impact: None — source code in a private SharePoint tenant poses no additional exposure
decisions.operational_impact: Low — artifacts are superseded by GitHub; removing them does not affect production
decisions.prerequisite: Verify no CI/CD pipeline reads from sites/projects before any deletion
decisions.consequence_of_deferral: Storage waste and ambiguity about canonical code location continues
decisions.approval_phrase: APPROVE FD-003 — archive and remove dev build artifacts from sites/projects (retain Team shell pending FD-006)

decisions.title: Sales Team and Voicemail Team — confirm need
decisions.plain_english_question: Is the Sales Team still used for collaboration (if not, should it be archived)? And does voicemail routing depend on the Voicemail Team identity (which determines whether the Team can be decoupled from routing and archived)?

voicemail.function: Voicemail routing (Teams calling / auto-attendant may depend on this Team identity)

decisions.why_this_exists: Sales: created for pricing/deal collaboration. Voicemail: created to support Teams calling voicemail delivery. Both are low-to-inactive on document activity.

recommendation.sales: If Sales collaboration has ended, ARCHIVE the Team and site. Pricing sheets can be moved to a shared library in marketing or support.
recommendation.voicemail: Do NOT archive until routing dependency is confirmed. If voicemail@jmerrill.pub shared mailbox can receive routing independently, decouple and archive the Team. If the Team identity is required by Teams calling, RETAIN.

alternatives.sales_retain: Retain Sales Team if active collaboration is expected to resume
alternatives.sales_archive: Archive Team/site/Group if Sales collaboration has definitively moved elsewhere
alternatives.voicemail_retain: Retain Voicemail Team if routing cannot be safely decoupled
alternatives.voicemail_decouple_archive: Decouple routing to shared mailbox, then archive Team

decisions.if_approved_sales_archive: Authorizes Wave 5 Step 1: archive Sales Team + Group + site (pricing sheets migrated first)
decisions.if_approved_voicemail_decouple: Authorizes Wave 5 Step 2: routing dependency confirmed removed, then archive Voicemail Team
decisions.if_deferred: Both Teams remain in low/inactive state with unclear destiny
decisions.operational_impact: CRITICAL for Voicemail — incorrect routing change could break voicemail delivery
decisions.prerequisite: Voicemail: confirm technical routing path before any action
decisions.consequence_of_deferral: Teams remain in ambiguous state; Voicemail routing risk remains undocumented
decisions.approval_phrase: APPROVE FD-004 — ARCHIVE Sales Team after pricing sheet migration; RETAIN Voicemail Team pending routing dependency confirmation

decisions.title: Seven shared mailboxes — classify each
decisions.plain_english_question: For each of the seven shared mailboxes below, is it: (A) actively receiving external email for a real organizational audience, (B) a retained alias that doesn't need active staffing, or (C) unused and removable?

current_state.already_classified: legal@, preneeds@, royalties@, submissions@, tech@, info@, no-reply@, notifications@, logging@ — all classified KEEP — CORE/SYSTEM

decisions.why_this_exists: These mailboxes were created for organizational communication roles. Usage metrics are unavailable (403), so active use must be confirmed by Jackie who knows which are actively managed.

recommendation.board: KEEP — CORE (Foundation governance credibility; board@ is a standard nonprofit identity)
recommendation.donations: KEEP — CORE (donor-facing; retiring donations@ creates external confusion)
recommendation.grants: KEEP — CORE (Foundation grants program; retiring grants@ may lose incoming applications)
recommendation.accounting: KEEP if actively used for financial correspondence; ALIAS if rarely used
recommendation.media: KEEP if press/PR inquiries are active; ALIAS if media contacts primarily reach the team another way
recommendation.volunteers: KEEP if volunteer coordination is active; ALIAS if volunteer management moved to another channel
recommendation.contacts: CONSOLIDATE into info@ if contacts@ overlaps with it; otherwise KEEP as a general intake alias

options_per_mailbox.KEEP_CORE: Receives external email, serves a distinct operational audience, or is an automation target
options_per_mailbox.KEEP_ALIAS: Retained as forwarding alias; not actively staffed; no external announcement needed
options_per_mailbox.RETIRE: No active use, no external audience, no automation dependency

decisions.if_approved: Authorizes Wave 4: process each mailbox per the approved disposition — alias setup, forwarding, or retirement with grace period
decisions.if_deferred: Mailbox estate remains partially unclassified; external parties may reach unmonitored inboxes
decisions.cost_impact: Shared mailboxes are typically unlicensed; minimal direct cost impact
decisions.security_impact: Unmonitored mailboxes with external exposure are a low-level risk if phishing or spoofing targets them
decisions.operational_impact: Retiring an active mailbox breaks incoming email from donors/grantors/press
decisions.prerequisite: None — Jackie's operational knowledge is the only evidence source needed
decisions.consequence_of_deferral: Some mailboxes may receive external email with no one monitoring; others may be unnecessarily active
decisions.approval_phrase: APPROVE FD-005 — [for each mailbox: KEEP-CORE / KEEP-ALIAS / RETIRE]

decisions.title: Projects Team — confirm ongoing collaboration need
decisions.plain_english_question: Is the Projects Team channel still actively used for planning and coordination (meetings, posts, task tracking), or has that collaboration moved to GitHub Issues/Projects or other tools?

current_state.collaboration_activity: Unknown — channel post/meeting activity not audited

decisions.why_this_exists: The Projects Team was created for cross-team project coordination. SharePoint content is stale dev artifacts (FD-003), but the Team channel itself may still be used for planning regardless of the document store.
decisions.recommendation: If active planning/coordination happens in the Projects channel (meetings, posts, task assignments): RETAIN the Team. If all coordination has moved to GitHub Issues/Projects: ARCHIVE the Team shell after FD-003 content cleanup.

alternatives.RETAIN: Projects Team is actively used for planning regardless of SharePoint content
alternatives.ARCHIVE: Projects collaboration has moved to GitHub/other; archive Team after FD-003 cleanup

decisions.if_approved_archive: Authorizes Wave 5 Step 3: archive Projects Team after FD-003 content cleanup completes
decisions.if_retained: Projects Team stays active; content cleanup (FD-003) is still authorized independently
decisions.if_deferred: Tied to FD-003 — both remain in ambiguous state
decisions.operational_impact: If archived prematurely, active planning space is lost
decisions.prerequisite: FD-003 decision context is helpful but FD-006 can be answered independently
decisions.consequence_of_deferral: Team remains in unclear state alongside stale content
decisions.approval_phrase: APPROVE FD-006 — ARCHIVE Projects Team (if collaboration has moved to GitHub) OR RETAIN Projects Team (if channel is actively used)
